the observed abundance ratios in UFDs and the MW halo are consistent with a scenario in which the VMP populations of both were enriched by prior generations of massive stars.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the MW halo and the small number of UFDs studied thus far appear to have been enriched by the same prior generations of stars, but with a significant difference in the total masses of those generations.

the observed abundance distributions for VMP stars in both the MW halo and UFDs can be explained by a single scenario, in which the VMP stars are the result of a prior generation of more massive stars that enriched the MW halo and the UFD stars are the result a prior generation of less massive stars that enriched their UFDs.
the UFDs are the best laboratories for testing the MDY for nc-elements, which are the most sensitive to the nature of the first generation of stars in the Universe.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the observed abundance distributions of VMP stars are not necessarily indicative of the enrichment history of their progenitors.
the abundance distributions of the UFDs are consistent with the MW halo, but with a different prior generation of progenitors.
a MDY is a viable explanation for the observed abundance distributions of VMP stars and that the nature of the progenitors of the MW and UFDs are not identical.
